_comment: The complete scoring + simulation model behind the platform. All formulas match the mockup exactly. Arsenal Score is a weighted sum of four pillars, each normalized to 0-100.

pillars.name: Adversary Exposure
pillars.note: Scored inversely: a HIGH pillar score means LOW exposure (good). Start at 100 and subtract penalties, then clamp: score = max(5, 100 - penalties). In the rankings UI, a low score renders with more red fill.
pillars.floor_note: DECIDED 2026-07-27: 5 is absolute zero for this pillar, not 0. The penalties below sum to 110 against a 100 start, so an unclamped worst case is -10 and would drag the weighted Arsenal Score negative. OPEN: docs/STRATEGY.md line 142 carries a DIFFERENT penalty table (Current Financial Ties -30, Historical Financial Ties -15, Supply Chain Dependency -25, Technology Transfer Risk -15, Personnel Affiliations -15) that sums to exactly 100. The two tables disagree on the categories themselves, not just the totals. Client decision, raised with the client 2026-07-28.

surge_simulation._comment: Deterministic stock-and-flow model. Run per munition over a fixed horizon. This is exactly what the Surge Simulator computes.
surge_simulation.day_indexing: DECIDED 2026-07-27: t = 1 is the first day of shooting. Inventory enters day 1 at starting_inventory_units, and day 1 is the first day both production and consumption apply. Every reported metric day counts from there. Reference implementation: docs/reference/sim.js.

production.during_ramp: production[t] = baseline × (1 + (maxMultiple - 1) × progress),  progress = min(1, (t - leadTime) / rampDur)

ramp_params_from_surge_score._comment: s = surge_score / 100. These map a company's surge score to how fast/high its production can ramp.

advanced_manufacturing_toggle._comment: When 'Activate Advanced Manufacturing' is ON, apply these modifiers to the base params.

output_metrics.meet_demand_day: first day production >= consumption (null if never)
output_metrics.replenish_day: first day inventory returns to starting level AFTER being drawn down below 98% (null if not within horizon)
output_metrics.drawn_down_flag: true once inventory drops below 98% of starting inventory

demand_profiles._comment: Piecewise functions of day t, keyed by SCENARIO ID (taiwan, korea, baltic, maritime, multi, epicfury) — one profile per scenario, NOT one per type. DECIDED 2026-07-27: the engine looks up by scenario id. An earlier version of this comment said the scenario type selects the profile, which was wrong in a way that mattered: there are six profiles and only three types, and korea and baltic are both typed 'grind' while behaving oppositely (korea's demand decays, baltic's rises). scenario_types below is a display label only and drives nothing.

scenario_types.shock: short, ferocious fight; magazine depth built pre-conflict decides the outcome (taiwan, multi)
scenario_types.grind: protracted attrition; surge ramps have time to overtake demand (korea, baltic, maritime)
scenario_types.replenish: fight ends fast; the contest is rebuilding the magazine (epicfury)
